REPORT
This Report of the Committee deals with the action taken by the Ministry of Home Affairs on the
recommendations contained in the Two Hundred Ninth Report of the Committee on Demands for Grants
(2018-19) of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The Two Hundred Ninth Report was presented to Rajya
Sabha/laid on the Table of Lok Sabha, on 13th March, 2018.
2. Action Taken Notes as received from the Ministry of Home Affairs in respect of the
recommendations contained in the Two Hundred Ninth Report have been categorized as follows:
Chapter I: The recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the Government:
Para Nos. 2.2.7, 2.3.2, 3.5.6, 3.6.7, 3.6.18, 4.3.5, 4.7.12, 5.17.4, 5.22.2 and 5.24.4 (of Two
Hundred Ninth Report)
Total recommendations - 10
The Committee is pleased to note that the Ministry has accepted its recommendations as
mentioned in Chapter-I of the Report.
Chapter II: The recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in
view of the Government's replies: Para Nos. 5.5.5, 5.11.3 and 5.12.2 ( ibid)
Total recommendations - 03
The Committee is convinced with the explanations furnished by the Ministry and, therefore,
does not want to pursue the recommendations further.
Chapter III: The recommendations/observations in respect of which the Committee is not satisfied
with the replies of the Ministry: Para Nos. 2.3.3, 3.1.7, 3.1.8, 3.3.4, 3.4.6, 3.4.9, 3.4.12, 4.2.6,
4.5.4, 4.6.5, 4.9.4, 5.3.2, 5.4.2, 5.5.2, 5.6.5, 5.7.3, 5.9.2, 5.10.3 and 5.23.2 ( ibid)
Total recommendations - 19
The Committee expresses its concern over the non-implementation of its recommendations
contained in Chapter-III and desires that the Ministry should furnish convincing action taken steps
in respect of those recommendations.
Chapter IV: The recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the Government
have not been received: Para Nos. 2.2.8, 2.2.9, 3.4.11, 3.5.3, 3.6.15, 3.7.4, 3.8.4, 3.8.5, 4.2.3,
4.4.3, 4.5.5, 4.8.10, 4.10.4, 5.6.3, 5.8.3, 5.12.1, 5.13.4, 5.14.4, 5.15.4, 5.15.5, 5.16.4, 5.19.3,
5.21.1, 5.25.4 and 5.26.3 ( ibid)
Total Recommendations - 25
In respect of 25 recommendations in Chapter-IV, the Ministry has either furnished interim
reply or couched its response in vague terms.
The Committee desires that the Ministry should furnish pointed and detailed Action Taken Notes
in respect of the observations/recommendations made in the Report.
3. The details of analysis of the ATNs have been cited in the succeeding chapters.

2
CHAPTER-I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN
ACCEPTED BY THE GOVERNMENT
1.1 ALLOCATIONS, PROJECTIONS AND VARIATION
Recommendation
1.1.1 The Committee notes that the allocation of capital component granted under Demand No. 48
pertaining to the police forces was reduced by more than 5% from 
` 11178.36 crore to ` 10604.78 crore
at RE stage in 2017-18. This reduction under this component points towards an un-healthy expenditure
trend. The Committee is aware that several projects of national importance such as border infrastructure,
police modernisation, NATGRID, etc. are being implemented under this head and efficient utilisation of
funds is required for timely implementation of these projects. The Committee, therefore, recommends that
the Ministry should streamline the procedures and strengthen the monitoring mechanism to achieve better
utilisation of funds under this head during FY 2018-19. (Para 2.2.7 of 209th Report)
Action Taken
1.1.2 Ministry of Home Affairs consists of two major Grants  viz.  Grant No.46- MHA and Grant No.48
-Police. Funds of ` 11178.36 crore was allocated under Capital Section of both the Grants taken together.
1.1.3 Major portion of the Capital Section is under Grant No.48-Police. Capital allocation under Grant
No.48-Police is mainly under Police Infrastructure and Border Infrastructure and Management.
1.1.4 Ministry had constituted a Committee under the Chairmanship of former Home Secretary
Shri Madhukar Gupta to suggest ways to strengthen border protection and address the issue of gaps and
vulnerability in border fencing along the India-Pakistan border. Less expenditure was incurred under
Indo-Pak Border as some of the projects were reviewed and re-prioritized.
1.1.5 In order to achieve better utilization of funds under Border Management and Infrastructure, regular
review meetings to monitor the expenditure on the ongoing projects in Indo-Pak and Indo-Bangladesh
borders are held with various executing agencies.
1.1.6 Further, fund of Coastal Security section was mainly for procurement of 225 boats sanctioned
under Phase-II of Coastal Security Section (CSS). However, the boats could not be procured during the
financial year 2017-18. Police Modernization (PM) Division of the Ministry is at an advanced stage for
award of contract for procurement of 225 boats sanctioned under Phase-II of the CSS. Fund of CS
section shall be utilized mainly for procurement of aforementioned boats in the FY 2018-19.
1.1.7 In order to reduce the time in processing of procurement related cases and to enhance the
capabilities of CAPFs to incur capital expenditure, the following steps have been taken:-
(i) Clubbing of Provisioning Sanction with Authorization. Now there are only two stages  i.e.
authorization-cum-provisioning sanction and expenditure sanction against earlier three stages
for procurement.
2

3
(ii) Power of approving Qualitative Requirements (QRs)/Trial Directives (TDs) has been delegated
to Directors General (DsG), CAPFs.
(iii) Trial of samples once conducted during the tender process for technical evaluation will have
validity of 1-2 years to avoid recurrent trials.
(iv) Delegated financial power of DsG , CAPFs has been enhanced from ` 1 crore to ` 2 crore
for procurement of items for trial purpose.
(v) Special DG/ADG in charge of Provisioning in CAPFs shall head the meeting of Tender
Purchase Committee (TPC) instead of DsG, CAPFs.
(vi) Delegated financial power of DsG, CAPFs has been further delegated to lower functionaries
(till the Commandant) for procurement of stores under the various provisioning heads.
(vii) DsG, CAPFs have been delegated financial power for procurement of motor vehicles for
their newly raised units/establishments up to ` 20 crore in each case.
(viii) The expenditure by CAPFs is closely monitored.
1.1.8 In addition to the submissions made above, it is submitted that the Ministry has recently enhanced
the limits for delegation of financial powers to Directors General/ Directors of CAPFs/ CPOs from
` 10 crore to ` 15 crore for Works to be executed by CPWD/ PWOs as per Rule, 133(2)&(3) of GFR,
2017 in consultation with IFAs and from ` 50 lakh to ` 1 crore for Minor Works (petty repairs of Non
Residential Buildings / Residential Buildings) as per Rule 133 (1) and 133 (2) & (3) of General Financial
Rules, 2017. A copy of the order is enclosed as Annexure-I.
1.1.9 It is further submitted that in order to expedite the expenditure including capital expenditure, the
Ministry regularly conducts expenditure review meetings at the highest level ( viz. Home Minister/ Home
Secretary/ Financial Advisor). The Ministry ensures that the budget controlling authorities of respective
organizations/Divisions under its control leave no stone unturned towards entire expenditure allocated for
the FY 2018-19.
1.1.10 The recommendation of the Committee has been noted for future compliance.
Further Recommendation
1.1.11 The Committee notes the measures taken by the Ministry to reduce the time in processing
of procurement related cases and to enhance the capabilities of CAPFs to incur capital expenditure.
The Committee, however, feels that specific measures need to be taken for different projects of
national importance such as border infrastructure, police modernisation, and NATGRID to reduce
procedural delays and improve fund utilization. The Committee, therefore, desires to be apprised
about any such specific measures taken under these projects.
1.2 Under-utilisation of Funds
Recommendation
1.2.1 The Committee notes that by 20th February, 2018 the Ministry was able to spend only 61.58 per
cent of the allocation granted under the capital component in RE 2017-18 under both the Demand Nos.

4
46 and 48. This was despite a reduction in allocation from ` 11,501.33 crore to ` 10,908.68 crore at
RE stage. The Committee fails to understand the reasons for this poor capital expenditure and wonders
as to how the Ministry would be able to spend more than 38 per cent of the allocation with just 40 days
remaining in the current financial year. The Committee fears that a large sum of capital funds may have
to be surrendered by the Ministry and it may subject them to further cuts. The Committee expresses its
displeasure at the poor capital expenditure by the Ministry and is of the view that year after year such
sub-optimal utilization of funds is simply inexcusable. The Committee recommends that the Ministry
should try to remove all operational bottlenecks and undertake corrective measures to address the issues
underlying the continued poor capital expenditure pattern. (Para 2.3.2  ibid )
Action Taken
1.2.2 Ministry of Home Affairs consists of two major Grants viz. Grant No. 46-Ministry of Home
Affairs and Grant No. 48-Police. The Capital Allocation under both the Grants for the FY was `11,501.33
crore which was reduced to `10,908.66 crore mainly due to slow pace of expenditure under Border
Infrastructure and Management Scheme of the Ministry and under provisioning heads of CAPFs.
1.2.3 The progress in expenditure of funds on Border Infrastructure Works is dependent on various
factors, viz., difficult terrain, non-availability of site due to pending land acquisition, public protests,
objection by Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), etc.
1.2.4 Less expenditure was incurred under India-Pakistan Border Works as some of the projects were
reviewed and re-prioritized on the recommendation of the Madhukar Gupta Committee Report.
1.2.5 It is further submitted that under Grant No. 46-MHA and Grant No. 48-Police, the Ministry has
been able to spend 99.22 % w.r.t. BE / RE under Grant No. 46 MHA and 105.21% w.r.t. BE and
99.72 % RE under Grant No. 48- Police of total (Revenue + Capital) funds allocated and as far as capital
expenditure is concerned, the Ministry has been able to achieve 93.20% w.r.t. RE under Grant No.
46- MHA and 99.45% w.r.t. RE during the FY 2017-18. Thus, the Ministry was able to utilize considerable
funds efficiently.
1.2.6 However, it is further submitted that in order to expedite the expenditure including capital expenditure,
the Ministry regularly conducts expenditure review meetings at the highest level ( viz. Home Minister/
Home Secretary/ Financial Advisor). The Ministry ensures that the budget controlling authorities of
respective organizations / Divisions under its control leave no stone unturned towards entire expenditure
allocated for the FY.
1.2.7 Further, as explained in the reply to Para No. 2.2.7, steps are being undertaken to enhance the
capabilities of CAPFs to incur capital expenditure both under Works and for procurement related activities.
1.2.8 However, the recommendation of the Committee has been noted for compliance. All efforts will
be made to remove the bottlenecks and procedural delays that have led to slow pace of expenditure.
Further Recommendation
1.2.9 The Committee notes that the Ministry was able to achieve significant fund utilization at
the end of fiscal year 2017-18. However, the Committee feels that the Ministry needs to obviate

5
the uneven distribution of fund utilisation pattern during the fiscal year and achieve near-
uniform utilization pattern throughout the year so that the necessary funds are not surrendered
at RE stage. The Committee, therefore, further recommends that the Ministry must undertake
proactive measures to achieve optimum utilization of funds during all four quarters of a fiscal
year.
1.3 Infrastructure for Disaster Management
Recommendation
1.3.1 The Committee is displeased to note the underutilization of funds allocated under the head
Infrastructure for Disaster Management. The Committee also takes note of the submission of the Ministry
regarding the delay in the commencement of the construction work, of south campus of the National
Institute of Disaster Management, due to which the funds could not be utilized. The Committee fails to
understand why the construction could not begin despite the demarcation of land for the purpose and
desires to be apprised about the reasons for this delay. The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends
that the Ministry should resolve the bottlenecks that have delayed the construction work and ensure that
the construction will commence at the earliest. (Para 3.5.6 ibid)
Action Taken
1.3.2 The DPR/cost estimate was approved in 2017-18 on 5th October, 2017. MoU has been signed
between NIDM and NBCC on 9th October, 2017. On completion of formalities of advance position,
filling of alienation form and demarcation of the land in 17th January, 2018 NBCC has been given the
go-ahead to start the construction of NIDM, Southern Campus. Mobilization of advance of `3.43 core
was released to NIDM on 23rd March, 2018. The advance can be released only after finanlization of
tender and award of work by NBCC as the exact value of tender cost and the cost put to tender would
be known only then Therefore, fund couldn't be utilized during FY-2017-18. Hon'ble Vice President of
India laid the foundation stone of NIDM Southern Campus on 22nd May, 2018.
Further Recommendation
1.3.3 The Committee while taking note of the reply hopes that the construction of NIDM would
be completed within the time frame.

2.1 SOURCES OF ENERGY
Recommendation
2.1.1 The Committee laments the fact that the A&N Islands still have to depend fully on the conventional
sources of energy for power generation. The Committee is of the considered view that the use of solar
energy for power generation must be intensively promoted taking into account the weather conditions of
the Islands. The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the UT Administration must undertake
requisite measures to ensure installation of roof-top solar power plants in all the buildings in the Islands
beginning with all public buildings. The Committee also recommends that the work pertaining to the
proposed energy management centre must be completed expeditiously. (Para 5.5.5 of 209th Report)
Action Taken
2.1.2 UT Administration is taking measures to ensure installation of roof-top solar power plants in all
the buildings. Action already taken in this regard is as follows:
(i) 1 MWp Roof top solar power plant on 15 govt. buildings are installed and all are in operation
since April, 2017. UT Administration will purchase power from SECI @ `4.64 per unit
through Power Purchase Agreement for 25 years. This Project has generated 858333 units
till March, 2018 which has saved 225424 litres of diesel amounting to `134.80 lakh (@`59.80
per litre).
(ii) Installation of grid connected 1-10 KWp Rooftop Solar Power plant in private domestic
residence is in progress by M/s Ujaas Energy Pvt. Ltd., Indore and till date a total capacity
of 22.11 KWp has been commissioned. The target is 2 MWp.
(iii) Installation of 3 MWp Solar Rooftop in Govt. buildings:- Power Purchase Agreement (PPA)
has been signed with M/s Mundra Solar Pvt. Ltd. on 22nd March, 2018 for grid connected
solar roof top on Govt. buildings.
2.1.3 Administration has signed agreement with Power Grid during November, 2017 for setting up of
Energy Management Centre. Power Grid is finalising tender. Administration will ensure that the proposed
energy management centre is completed expeditiously.
Further Recommendation
2.1.4 The Committee notes the progress made in projects pertaining to installation of rooftop
solar power plants in private domestic residences and in Government buildings.

3.1 UNDERUTILISATION OF FUNDS
Recommendation
3.1.1 The Committee takes note of the sub-optimal expenditure incurred by most of the Governments of
UTs. The Committee is aware that the Union Territories have been pleading for more funds every fiscal
year for developmental activities. However, the trend of expenditure is not convincing enough to justify
the demands for higher allocations. The Committee fears that unless the Union Territories establish
strong fund utilization credentials, their demands for higher allocations may not be acceded to by the
Ministry of Finance. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Union Territories must demonstrate
a strong conviction for achieving optimal fund utilization in every quarter . The Committee also recommends
that the Ministry of Home Affairs may review the fund utilization status of every UT on a monthly basis
and implement corrective measures in a proactive manner. (Para 2.3.3 of 209th Report)

to establish a robust mechanism to improve their consumption capacity for achieving optimal fund
utilization quarter-wise and also review the fund utilization status on a monthly basis.

The action taken by MHA is to strongly advise the UT Administrations to follow the direction for
strict compliance. But the recommendations of the Committee was for the MHA to ensure that
the fund utilization status of every UT be reviewed on a monthly basis and corrective measures
are taken in proactive manner. The Committee, therefore, reiterates its recommendation.

3.8 Schemes for Safety of Women
Recommendation
3.8.1 The Committee is surprised to note that the allocations made for Schemes for Safety of Women
has been drastically cut down from 
`313.30 crore at BE 2017-18 to just `81.75 crore at BE 2018-19
which is supposed to be spent by all the States and Union Territory Governments, including the Delhi
Police. The Committee is disappointed that the allocated amount of ` 22.69 crore (capital) could not
be utilised completely due to which the allocation got substantially decreased to `7.87 crore in RE
2017-18. The Committee strongly disapproves of this lack of seriousness in strengthening the safety and
security of women in the country. The Committee wishes to remind the Ministry that Nirbhaya Fund was
intended to implement schemes which are technology-driven and which will significantly enhance the
security of women. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry should desist from allocating
funds, which are granted under the Nirbhaya Fund, for the purposes that can be covered by normal
spending. The Committee also recommends that at least one scheme should be implemented in every city
under the Nirbhaya Fund to significantly enhance the security of women. (Para 4.9.4 ibid)
Action Taken
3.8.2 The Government places the highest priority to address the issue of rising crimes against women.
The allocation for 'Schemes of Safety of Women', BE 2017-18 was ` 313.30 crore. It includes ` 84.40
crore for Emergency Response Support System (ERSS), ` 200 crore for Cyber Crime Prevention against
Women and Children (CCPWC) and ` 28.90 crore for Schemes related to Delhi Police.
3.8.3 At the Revised Estimate stage, an amount of ` 76 crore was allotted for Emergency Response
Support System (ERSS). The ERSS project is to introduce nationwide single emergency number '112'
backed by Computer Aided Dispatch (CAD). During the period 2016-17 and 2017-18 funds have been
released to States and UTs for implementation of the same. Therefore, since most of the expenditure out
of the approved outlay under the scheme has already been incurred upto 2017-18, only a small amount
is required during 2018-19 for the balance activities. As such, this decrease in allocation cannot be
regarded as decreased attention towards the cause of safety of women.
3.8.4 In fact, the Government has recently identified eight large cities for implementation of Safe-City
Projects for women at a total cost of ` 2919.55 crore. The cities identified are Delhi, Chennai, Kolkata,
Mumbai, Bangalore, Hyderabad, Lucknow & Ahmedabad. It is expected that the cities shall start
implementing their plan in the fiscal year 2018-19.
3.8.5 It would thus be seen that there is no reduction in allotments for the purpose, on the other hand
there is a marked increase in allotments.
3.8.6 Further, under the Central Victim Compensation Fund (CVCF) Scheme, financial assistance of
` 200 crore as one-time grant has been sanctioned from Nirbhaya Fund and allocated to States / UTs

25
for compensating women victims on crimes committed against victims of acid attacks, rape, trafficking
etc. The entire amount of 200 crore has been disbursed to all the States/UTs during the financial year
2016-17. States/ UTs have been reminded for furnishing of Utilization Certificate for the amount received
by them under CVCF as a one-time grant.
3.8.7 The project of new office Building for office of Special Unit for Women & Children (SPUW AC)
and Special Unit for North East Region (SPUNER) at Nanak Pura, New Delhi under the Scheme for
Safety of Women (Funded by Nirbhaya Fund) has been awarded to M/s UPRNN. The building plan was
released on 21st September, 2017. During the financial year 2017-18, ` 21.17 crore was allocated under
the scheme for Safety of Women (Nirbhaya Fund), out of which ` 2.35 crore (Mobilisation Advance)
was released to M/s UPRNN on 9th August, 2017 and balance fund of `18.82 crore was surrendered
since the finalization of tender was under process. Hence funds could not be utilized due to no demand
by Executing Agency. Now, the work is likely to be awarded to the contractor shortly.
3.8.8 Under the head "Nirbhaya Fund" a budget of ` 35 lakh was allotted to this unit during the
financial year 2017-18 for procurement of Cyber equipment. Out of ` 35 lakh allocated, budget of
` 32,04,483/- was utilized during the financial year 2017-18. An amount of ` 2,95,517/- could not be
utilized due to technical difficulties occurring on GeM portal, though the expenditure sanction of the
competent authority was received.
Further Recommendation
3.8.9 The Committee takes note of the reply of the Ministry that the decreased allocation made
for 'Schemes of Safety of Women' was primarily because most of the expenditure out of the
approved outlay for Emergency Response Support System had already been incurred upto
2017-18. The Committee, however, feels that the Ministry should have been more proactive in
finding new technology-driven projects that could have been implemented during the current
fiscal year. The Committee feels that Ministry should identify such innovative projects for
funding and implementation. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry should
undertake sincere efforts to identify innovative technology-driven projects that can enhance the
safety of women, and seek additional funds for their implementation.
3.8.10 The Committee also observes that ````` 200 crore have been sanctioned as one-time grant for
Central Victim Compensation Fund (CVCF) Scheme for compensating women victims of acid
attacks, rape, trafficking, etc. The Committee appreciates the necessity and significance of the
CVCF Scheme, however, the Committee feels that this Scheme could have been funded from
sources other than Nirbhaya Fund, which was meant for funding initiatives aimed at enhancing
the safety and security for women in the country. The Committee feels that sanctioning funds
from Nirbhaya Fund for schemes pertaining to compensation would render the entire fund as a
fund for merely disbursal and would not have a desired impact at the ground level in enhancing
the security scenario for the women. The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the
Ministry should desist from sanctioning funds for such Schemes from Nirbhaya Fund and adhere
to the original purpose of Nirbhaya Fund. The Committee is also of the firm view that Nirbhaya
Fund should not be used for construction of buildings. Funds for construction of buildings should

26
come from other sources and not from the Nirbhaya Fund. Such allocations virtually defeat the
purpose of the Nirbhaya Fund.

3.15.2 There are many nallahs including few rivers such as Rangat river and Kalpong river in the North
& Middle Andaman which carry huge discharge during monsoon and banks get eroded. It is also a usual
phenomenon that these nallahs and river change their course which ultimately erodes new areas on its
bank. Due to this erosion of bank over the years, a considerable quantum of agricultural land belonging
to farmers/ settlers of the area has been lost besides posing danger to many of the structures such as
buildings, roads and bridges, etc.
3.15.3 In order to save some of the buildings, road and bridges which were vulnerable to these bank
erosions in the past, CC/RCC walls were provided apart crates of gabions filled with stone boulders on
those places, which are most needed due to fund constraints. However, there is a growing demand from
PRI members of the area and also from the Hon'ble MP to provide protective measures along the banks

31
which passes through agricultural lands and habitat area to protect the land and other structures situated
along the bank.

concluded that gabion crates filled with stone boulder is the best way to protect bank erosion. Protection
measure would cost around `9.17 crore per kilometre.
3.15.5 As regarding ascertaining the quantum of protective measures, the Agriculture Department has
already undertaken a survey of agricultural land requires such protective measures. The outcome of the
survey duly verified by the Revenue Department have been received only for Diglipur Tehsil and the

The Committee may be apprised as and when adequate funds for building infrastructure
facilities for NDRF Academy in Nagpur and 11 Bn NDRF, Hollangi in Arunachal Pradesh are
sanctioned. (Para 4.3.3)
NATIONAL CYCLONE RISK MITIGATION PROJECT (NCRMP)
The Committee notes the slow progress in the execution of Multipurpose Cyclone Shelters
(MPCS) and observes that during the first half of 2018, construction of not a single MPCS has
been completed. The Committee feels that such a slow pace is not acceptable and the Ministry
of Home Affairs seriously needs to fast-track the construction. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the Project Steering Committee and the Project Oversight committee should
meet on a monthly basis to strengthen the monitoring of projects. (Para 4.4.3)
The Committee also observes the time period of completion of Multipurpose Cyclone
Shelters (MPCS) i.e. 15 to 18 months and feels that the Ministry may not be able to complete
all the MPCS by March, 2020, even if the construction of all the remaining shelters has been
taken up by the end of December, 2018. The Committee, therefore, recommends that all the
States may be advised about this aspect and may be urged to complete the construction process.
The Committee desires to be apprised about the number of MPCS that have been completed.
(Para 4.4.4)
SPECIAL INDUSTRY INITIATIVE FOR JAMMU AND KASHMIR
The Committee desires to be apprised whether the UDAAN scheme has been granted
extension from December 2018 till 2020. (Para 4.5.3)
HOME GUARDS
The Committee takes note of the statement of the Ministry that Home Guards is a state
subject. But the Committee feels that MHA should continue pursuing state governments for
implementing the Supreme Court's order and lead by example by implementing it in all the UTs.
The Ministry should convene a meeting of all the States/UTs under the Chairmanship of Home
Secretary to discuss the pitiable condition of the Home Guards and seek reasons for not
implementing Supreme Court's order. The Committee also recommends that the division concerned
of MHA may send a monthly reminder on this issue and obtain regular status of action taken
in this matter. (Para 4.6.6)

ANNEXURE-II
Two officers from FFR Division lead by Joint Secretary (FFR) visited Cooch Behar from 9th
November, 2017 to 12th November, 2017 to take stock of condition of enclave dwellers and review
overall implementation of the package.
Out of 51 erstwhile Bangladeshi enclaves that integrated in mainland, officers randomly visited
JyotNizam enclave settlement falling under jurisdiction of Mekhligang along with Block Development
Officer and their field units.
As per provision of the scheme up-gradation of infrastructure such as Pucca road, kutcha road,
drain, culverts, bridges, mark II tubewell, piped water supply, deep tubewell, primary school, high
school, health sub centre, anganwari centre, household electricity etc are to be developed in 51 former
Bangladeshi enclaves in India that have been integrated into mainland.
A meeting was arranged with BDO, Mekhligang to discuss development work in their jurisdiction.
Site visit reveal that the District authority has so far completed work of electrification, water supply,
drainage, playground, construction of toilet and upgraded school namely no. 1 Dwarikamari Government
Primary School falling under their jurisdiction. The people are feeling comfortable in terms of facilities
and safely being provided by the State Government after exchange of enclaves. The officials also visited
the Ratanpur Boarder Out Post (BOP) to know security situations posts exchange of enclaves between
India and Bangladesh. The Wire fencing has been done in the area and BSF officials expressed their ease
to guard this augmented.
Out of three resettlement camp in Cooch Bihar District, 104 dwelling units each covering 750 sqft
area are being built for returnees from erstwhile Indian enclaves in Bangladesh falling under jurisdiction
of Haldibari. Three blocks each having 8 flats in doubled storied buildings have been completed and work
in remaining blocks is in progress. These resettlement camps are to be equipped with basic common
infrastructure like school with play-ground, aganwadi centre, health centre, community shelter etc. in
totality. The district authority assured to complete the work within stipulated time.
Temporary settlement camp situated in Haldibari provides accommodation of 96 returnees from
erstwhile Indian enclaves in Bangladesh. The returnees were initially given gruel kitchen for 30 days.
Thereafter, dry ration such as rice, dal, salt, milk powder, mustard oil, kerosene oil are being provided
to them. These returnees have also been covered under Khadya Sathi Scheme for making provisions in
coming days. These people have been provided Indian citizenship, MNREGA card, EPIC card, Aadhaar
card, Bank Accounts etc. to facilitate their living in the country. State Government is also imparting skill
development training to these people to enable them to earn livelihood and ameliorate their financial
conditions.
Site visit of construction of bridge on river Teesta connecting Haldibari to Mekhliganj divulges very
sluggish progress of work. Out of total 60 pillars, embankment and culverts proposed to be constructed
over river, work on 10 pillars have started. The undertaking agency and state officials explained difficulties
being faced by them in construction of bridge over river. The encompassing area remains inundated
almost half of a year. Authority concerned assured that all difficulties have been sidelined and work will
be completed within stipulated time.

REPORT
The Action Taken Report of the Committee deals with the action taken by the Ministry of
Development of North Eastern Region on the recommendations contained in the Two Hundred Tenth
Report of the Committee on Demands for Grants (2018-19) of the Ministry. The Two Hundred Tenth
Report was presented to Rajya Sabha /laid on the Table of Lok Sabha, on 4th April, 2018.
2. Action Taken Notes as received from the Ministry of DoNER in respect of the recommendations
contained in the Two Hundred Tenth Report have been categorized as follows:
Chapter I: The Recommendations/Observations, which have been accepted by the Government:
Para Nos. 2.6.4, 2.9.7, 2.10.8, 2.11.10, 2.12.3, 2.14.8, 2.19.6, 2.22.6, 3.11.12, 3.11.13 and 3.15.4
(of Two Hundred Tenth Report)
Total recommendations-11
The Committee is pleased to note that the Ministry has accepted its recommendations as
mentioned in Chapter-I of the Report.
Chapter II: The Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue
in view of the Government's replies: Para Nos. 2.2.2, 2.5.5, 2.9.5, 2.25.8, 3.1.6 and 3.10.2, ( ibid)
Total recommendations - 6
The Committee is convinced with the explanations furnished by the Ministry and, therefore,
does not want to pursue the recommendations further.
Chapter III: The Recommendations/Observations in respect of which the Committee is not satisfied
with the replies of the Ministry: Para Nos. 2.9.9, 2.11.11, 2.18.4, 2.18.5, 2.21.6, 2.21.10, 2.23.8,
3.6.3, 3.6.6, 3.6.14, 3.8.3, 3.11.11, 3.12.8, 3.13.3, 3.14.5 and 3.16.4 ( ibid)
Total recommendations - 16
The Committee expresses its concern over the non-implementation of its recommendations
contained in Chapter-III and desires that the Ministry should furnish convincing action taken steps
in respect of those recommendations.
Chapter IV: The Recommendations/Observations in respect of which final replies of the Government
have not been received: Para Nos. 2.4.4, 2.8.11, 2.20.5, 2.24.11, 3.6.10, 3.7.16, 3.9.2, 3.11.14
and 3.11.15 ( ibid)
Total Recommendations - 9
The Committee desires that the Ministry should furnish pointed and detailed Action Taken Notes
in respect of the Observations/Recommendations made in all chapters of the Report.
3. The details of the ATNs have been analyzed in the succeeding chapters.

2
CHAPTER-I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN
ACCEPTED BY THE GOVERNMENT
1.1 SECRETARIAT
Recommendation
1.1.1 The Committee emphasizes that all instructions issued by the Ministry of Finance from time to time
on economizing and rationalizing of expenditure should be scrupulously followed by the Ministry of
DoNER. (Para 2.6.4 of 210th Report)
Action Taken
1.1.2 The recommendations of the Committee have been noted for compliance.
1.2 SPECIAL DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS
Recommendation
1.2.1 The Committee takes note of the submission of the Secretary, NEC that the moment the NEC
transfers the money to the CPWD, it would be assumed that it has been spent. The Committee finds this
response of the NEC to be very unsatisfactory. The Committee observes that if the NEC transfers the
money in the month of February or March, the CPWD will find it difficult to spend and most probably
it will lapse, which is highly objectionable. The Committee also observes that simply transferring the
funds does not mean that it would be spent by the end of the Financial Year for the intended purpose
and recommends that this distinction should be clearly defined and taken into account in future projects.
(Para 2.9.7 ibid)
Action Taken
1.2.2 The recommendations of the Committee are noted for compliance. The matter is related to the
scheme of North Eastern Road Sector Development Scheme (NERSDS). The latest sequence of events
are as follows:-
(i) Continuation of the scheme beyond March, 2017 was recommended by EFC in December,
2017 with an allocation of ` 1000.00 crore, which has been approved by the Cabinet in its
meeting held on 28th March, 2018.
(ii) In the meantime the preparation of the DPRs for the identified projects was assigned to BBJ
and CPWD.
(iii) NEC signed MoU with CPWD on 21st February, 2018 for implementation of the Scheme.
Therefore, fund amounting to ` 138.00 crore was transferred to CPWD.
(iv) However, now with the approval of competent authority in place, the situation shall be
avoided in future.
2

3
1.3 Central Pool of Resources for North East and Sikkim
Recommendation
1.3.1 The Committee expresses its concern over the reduction in allocation under the capital head to
` 175.00 crore at RE stage in 2017-18 against ` 369.00 crore allocated in BE 2017-18. Though the
actual expenditure was ` 190.00 crore in 2016-17. The Committee takes note of the plea that the Ministry
of Railways could absorb the fund to the tune of ` 57.63 crore only against the allocation of ` 260.00
crore on Akhaura-Agartala Rail link project as approved by the Central Monitoring Committee (CMC)
in BE 2017-18 on account of delay in handing over land, exceptionally high rain fall during the year
and delay in shifting of electrical utilities by the State Government. However, the Committee has been
assured that the Akhaura-Agartala Rail Link project would be completed without time and cost overruns.
The Committee hopes that the project would receive the highest priority and be completed without time
and cost overruns. (Para 2.10.8 ibid)
Action Taken
1.3.2 The recommendations of the Committee have been noted for compliance.
Further Recommendation
1.3.3 The Committee notes the reply

Recommendation

speedy implementation viz., just-in-time release of funds by which an initial token amount of

lakh is released for tendering of works and balance amount of first installment is released only after
receipt of letter of award of the contract; number of installments reduced to two as against the earlier
practice of three installments; maximum expenditure of outlay against ongoing projects; online submission
of requisite documents, which shortened processing period; regular review meetings and campaigning in
the States to expedite timely completion of projects. The Committee appreciates the measures taken by
the Ministry of DoNER and recommends that all projects undertaken under NLCPR and projects undertaken
by the NEC should be completed within the stipulated time frame. (Para 2.11.10 ibid)
Action Taken
1.4.2 Utmost efforts will be made to complete all projects undertaken under NLCPR within the stipulated

the efficiency of the new guidelines. (Para 2.12.3 ibid)

1.6 NER Livelihood (EAP) Project (NERLP)
Recommendation
1.6.1 The Committee feels that the major impediment in the implementation of NERLP is the absence
of institutionalised credit to SHGs. The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that steps be taken
for improving the bank linkage of the SHGs. Concerted efforts such as signing of MOUs with banks,
provision of Bank Mitras and appointment of Banking Correspondents for serving in the areas not
covered by banking services must be made. The Committee hopes that the projects undertaken under the
NERLP would prove effective in increasing employment opportunities, improving rural livelihoods, etc.
in selected identified districts of Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tripura. (Para 2.14.8 ibid)
Action Taken
1.6.2 Following the North East Financial Inclusion Conference held at National Institute of Rural
Development (NIRD) on the 28th November 2017, and with active persuasive role played by Ministry
of DoNER, the first MoU was signed between IDBI and NERLP during the same conference. Thereafter
NERLP is making continuous efforts for credit linkage of the SHGs that are formed by the project.
1.6.3 Out of 28,144 SHGs 27,072 (96%) SHGs have opened bank account in different bank branches
and remaining are in progress. Opening a savings bank account is the primary criteria to avail credit from
the banks. Hence, NERLP is doing its best on this aspect.
1.6.4 The following steps are being taken for bank linkages of the SHGs:-
(i) MoUs have been signed with IDBI (Sikkim), Tripura Grameen Bank (TGB), Tripura State
Cooperative Bank (TSCB), Mizoram Rural Bank (MRB) for effective credit delivery. More

branches of these two districts very soon.

infrastructures from the project. Accordingly, the BCs will be placed in the unbanked areas
of Sikkim. Efforts are being made to identify more BCs in the unbanked areas of all the
four project states.

2.5 Vision 2020
Recommendation
2.5.1 The Committee takes note of the thrust areas of Vision 2020 Document which inter-alia includes
inclusive growth, poverty eradication, rural sector, infrastructure, human resource development, banking,
industries and tourism. As the year 2020 is approaching, the Committee feels that progress of the projects,
undertaken under Vision 2020 Document, should be reviewed by Ministry of DoNER along with the
Ministries concerned to assess the current status vis-a-vis the set targets and make requisite policy
modification/intervention to ensure their completion within the stipulated time frame to achieve the
objectives of mission of Vision 2020. (Para 3.1.6 ibid)
Action Taken
2.5.2 NER Vision 2020 document, prepared after extensive public consultations held in all the 8 States
of NER and discussions in the 55th NEC Plenary held in December, 2007 was adopted in the following

11
Plenary Session held at Agartala on 13th May, 2008. The Vision 2020 document is a statement of the
felt requirements and needs of the people of the North Eastern Region of India. It included sectoral
strategies for areas such as inclusive growth, poverty eradication, rural sector, infrastructure, human
resource development, banking, industries and tourism. It identified a six-pronged strategy to bring about
inclusive development, help alleviate poverty and ensure reasonable standards of living for every family.
The six components of the strategy can be summarised as under:-
(i) Empowerment of the people to maximise self-governance and participatory development
through grassroots planning.
(ii) Expanding opportunities for a majority of the people living in villages through rural development
initiatives.
(iii) Developing sectors with comparative advantage so as to utilize the resources of the region
productively for the benefit and welfare of the people.
(iv) Human development including health and creating and building capacity of governance and
development institutions both in the private and public sectors.
(v) Creation of an investment climate by providing state-of-the-art infrastructure, especially
connectivity both, within the region and with the rest of the world.
(vi) Generating adequate resources for public investment in infrastructure, implementing a
framework for private participation in augmenting infrastructure
2.5.3 Since the adoption of the Vision 2020, NEC has referred to the document while planning the
various developmental strategies of the NER.
2.5.4 While PRI institutions exist in most North Eastern States and 14th Finance Commission had made
substantial fund devolution for the 3rd Tier of the Government. Provisions contained in parts IX and IXA
of the Constitution providing for Panchayats and Municipalities respectively, exempt certain areas from
the applicability of these parts. Besides, there are excluded areas under State Legislation eg Manipur Hill
areas. The amendment of the Sixth Schedule of Constitution for extending certain features of PRIs is
under consultation by Ministry of Parchayati Raj Institution (MOPRI) and Ministry of Tribal Affairs with
the concerned State Governments and the endeavour is for early alignment of Central and State Laws
with Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act (PESA). Efforts are also on by MOPRI to pursue
action to integrate traditional institutions with the formal system. The Home Ministry has launched
development packages in some Sixth Schedule districts of Assam which are being implemented by M/
o DONER. Thirteenth Finance Commission had made devolutions to local bodies in sixth Schedule and
other excluded areas for subjects assigned to PRIs. While the 14th Finance Commission did not devolve
funds to excluded areas, it had highlighted the need to address the development needs of these areas in
a focused manner. Accordingly, Ministry of Finance had made provisions for these areas. Ministry of
DONER and NEC have 25 per cent allocation for shelf of projects in these areas. Ministry of DoNER
has recently initiated a pilot in remote hilly district, namely, Tamenglong district in Manipur.
2.5.5 Several Sectoral Ministries are running livelihood initiatives such as Gram Swarojgar Yojana of
Ministry of Panchayati Raj, MSME Schemes, National rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM) of MORD and

12
Urban Livelihood Mission of HUA, Livelihood Schemes of Ministry of tribal Affairs. Besides initiatives
such as Start-Up India and North East Industrial Development Scheme (NEIDS), 2017 to promote
employment through entrepreneurship.
2.5.6 The North Eastern Region Community Resource Management Project (NERCORMP) is a joint
livelihood project of North Eastern Council (NEC), Ministry of DoNER, Government of India and
International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) running under North Eastern Region Community
Resource Management Society (NERCRMS) (A registered Society under North Eastern Council). The
objective of NERCORMP is to improve the livelihoods of vulnerable groups in a sustainable manner
through improved management of their resource base in a way that contributes to preservation and
restoration of the environment.
2.5.7 NERCORMP operates in four (4) States covering ten (10) Districts viz: Assam (Karbi Anglong and
Dima Hasao), Manipur (Ukhrul, Senapati, Chaurachandpur and Chandel), Meghalaya (West Garo Hills and

Management Groups (NaRMGs). Through the support from NERCORMP, these Community Based
Organisations (CBOs) are working together with all the community members to bring about a sustainable
livelihood for the village and society as a whole.
2.5.8 Ministry of DoNER is implementing World Bank assisted North East Rural Livelihood Project
(NERLP) in the four States namely Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tripura for a period of 5 years
(extended upto March, 2019) with a total project cost of ` 683.2 crore wherein Gol's contribution is
10 per cent. The objective of the project is to improve rural livelihoods, especially that of women,
unemployed youth and the most disadvantaged in the four participating North East States. It is envisaged
to increase the income of the targeted people by 30 per cent by the end of the project.
2.5.9 In the remaining districts of the NE, Deendayal Antodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods
Mission (DAY-NRLM), a flagship programme of the Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD), that seeks

to meet the needs of smaller entrepreneurs in the remote areas of the Region. Till 31st January, 2018,

MFIs/NBFCs from 8 North Eastern States. These microfinance intermediaries reached out to more than

the programme will be unsatisfactory unless the projects are approved on time. The Committee finds it
difficult to understand that the Ministry expects to implement the Programme Component merely by
transferring the funds when the projects have not been even granted approval by the Ministry. The
Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the preparation of DPR of seven roads and two bridges
in Sikkim by the BBJ and preparation of DPR of eight roads by the CPWD must be expedited so that
all the projects under the programme component of the NERSDS are approved in time, funds are
allocated/released and all the projects are implemented within a specified time frame without any cost
overrun. (Para 2.18.5 ibid)
Action Taken
3.3.7 On preparation of DPRs, the NEC has already submitted 5 roads/bridges projects in Sept 2018.
The proposals are under examination in the Ministry and are likely to be considered for sanction by the
Competent Authority. As already submitted, the works for these projects can be awarded by December,

20
2018 so as to start works in the next working season i.e. after December, 2018 and fund will be utilized
accordingly.
Further Recommendation
3.3.8 The Committee observes with concern that against the preparation of DPR of seven roads
and two bridges in Sikkim by the BBJ and preparation of DPR of eight roads by the CPWD, NEC
has submitted only 5 roads/bridges project till September 2018. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the Ministry of DoNER must co-ordinate with State Government concerned and
expedite preparation of DPRs of all projects of programme component of NERSDS and get
approval of competent authority expeditiously so that all projects are completed within set
timeframe and estimated cost.
3.4 Dima Hasao Autonomous T erritorial Council (DHATC)
Recommendation
3.4.1 The Committee is dismayed with the working of the Dima Hasao Territorial Council as the Council

crore per annum) over and above the Plan fund, but Dima Hasao Council could spend ` 23.37 only

to expedite the process. As a result of these pro active actions, the State Govt. has recently submitted

3.4.3 The Committee appreciates the initiatives taken by the Ministry of DoNER in coordinating
with State Government of Assam for timely formulation of infrastructure projects of Dima Hasao
Autonomous Territorial Council (DHATC), however, all this could result in the State Government
submitting the utilisation certificates (UCs) for ````` 18.30 crore only. The Committee, therefore,
feels that further efforts of the Ministry is required to encourage the State Government of
Assam to prepare DPRs for more infrastructural projects so that the entire allocated amount is
utilized and UCs are submitted in time.

21
Recommendation
3.4.4 The Committee is constrained to express its deep displeasure over the dismal performance of Dima
Hasao Territorial Council (DHTC) and Karbi Anglong Autonomous Territorial Council (KAATC) due to
low absorption capacity of these autonomous territorial councils. The Committee finds that there are
serious procedural lacunae in the functioning mechanism of both the Councils, which were created to give
autonomy to the tribals for their upliftment, but unfortunately, the councils are not able to absorb the
allocated amount on development activities. The Committee fails to understand the reason. When Bodoland
Territorial Council (BTC) can absorb all its allocated funds within the stipulated time, what holds up
the other territorial councils to follow the footsteps of BTC? The Committee is of the opinion that there
seems to be no mechanism in place to expedite the development process by preparing schemes, taking

situation of utilization of funds may improve in the current financial year onward.
Further Recommendation
3.4.6 The Committee understands that there is institutional framework in place but the outcome
has not been encouraging so far as otherwise the entire allocated funds for infrastructure
projects for Dima Hasao Territorial Council (DHTC) and Karbi Anglong Autonomous Territorial
Council (KAATC) could have been utilized optimally. The Committee is dissatisfied with the reply
of the Ministry and recommends that the Ministry of DoNER needs to furnish an explanation on
the reasons for low absorption capcity of DHTC and KAATC, and the measures taken by the
Ministry of DoNER and the State Government of Assam to remove the bottlenecks in
implementation of development projects. The Committee also reiterates its recommendation that
DHTC and KAATC must expedite the development process in their restrictive territory by
preparing schemes, seeking approval of DPRs and execute all undertaken projects in a time
bound manner .
3.5 North East Development Finance Corporation (NEDFi)
Recommendation
3.5.1 The Committee appreciates the performance of the North East Development Finance Corporation
(NEDFi) for promotion of MSME and micro finance sector which, no doubt, contribute towards more

the pace of entrepreneurship development, setting up of Business Facilitation Centres and undertaking
other developmental and promotional activities. (Para 2.23.8 ibid)

3.5.2 The annual budgetary allocations of fund received by NEDFi since the financial year 2002-03, are
fully utilized for disbursement to MSME and Micro finance projects. Besides, the Corporation, from its
own resources, undertakes several initiatives/ activities towards promotion and development of MSME
& Micro finance sectors in the region, in line with the terms and conditions stipulated in the MoU signed
with the Ministry of DoNER. The annual budgetary support from the Govt. of India was extended to
NEDFi since the beginning of the 10th Five Year Plan. With that support, NEDFi witnessed rapid growth
in its operation by extending financial assistance to more than 5400 no. of projects with total sanctions
and disbursement of around ` 4692.00 crore and ` 3616.00 crore respectively, facilitating capital

the Region for accelerating industrial development. The Corporation is continuously exploring various
avenues for raising its resources to meet the demand of assistance generated in the region. Since, the

Namchi, Tarku-Damthang-Namchi and Nayabazaar-Legship had begun way back in 2013. Even after the
passage of nearly 5 years, none of the stretches is near the completion stage. These are major roads that
provide connectivity in the South and West Sikkim Districts and are important for both the local
population and incoming tourists. The Nayabazar-Legship road, having a length of mere 24 km., has

an audit of construction activities of these roads and must seek explanation from the Sikkim PWD for
the extremely snail-pace of the works pertaining to these roads. The Committee also recommends that
accountability may be fixed/enforced for this non-performance and remedial measures should be taken
urgently to expedite the completion of these Roads. The Committee desires to be apprised of the action
taken in this regard. (Para 3.6.3 ibid)

approval of competent authority expeditiously so that all projects are completed within set
timeframe and estimated cost. (Para 3.3.8)
DIMA HASAO AUTONOMOUS TERRITORIAL COUNCIL (DHATC)
The Committee appreciates the initiatives taken by the Ministry of DoNER in coordinating
with State Government of Assam for timely formulation of infrastructure projects of Dima Hasao
Autonomous Territorial Council (DHATC), however, all this could result in the State Government
submitting the utilisation certificates (UCs) for ````` 18.30 crore only. The Committee, therefore,
feels that further efforts of the Ministry is required to encourage the State Government of
Assam to prepare DPRs for more infrastructural projects so that the entire allocated amount is
utilized and UCs are submitted in time. (Para 3.4.3)
DIMA HASAO AUTONOMOUS TERRITORIAL COUNCIL (DHATC)
The Committee understands that there is institutional framework in place but the outcome
has not been encouraging so far as otherwise the entire allocated funds for infrastructure
projects for Dima Hasao Territorial Council (DHTC) and Karbi Anglong Autonomous Territorial
Council (KAATC) could have been utilized optimally. The Committee is dissatisfied with the reply
of the Ministry and recommends that the Ministry of DoNER needs to furnish an explanation on
the reasons for low absorption capcity of DHTC and KAATC, and the measures taken by the
Ministry of DoNER and the State Government of Assam to remove the bottlenecks in
implementation of development projects. The Committee also reiterates its recommendation that
DHTC and KAATC must expedite the development process in their restrictive territory by
preparing schemes, seeking approval of DPRs and execute all undertaken projects in a time
bound manner. (Para 3.4.6)
NORTH EAST DEVELOPMENT FINANCE CORPORATION (NEDFI)
The Committee is constrained to express its displeasure over the reduction of annual
budgetary allocation of the Central Government to the North East Development Finance
Corporation (NEDFi) from ````` 60.0 crore to ````` 30.00 crore since the financial year 2015-16. Keeping
in view the role of the key driver of equitable economic development and inclusive growth by
NEDFi through promotion of MSME and micro-finance, the Committee had recommended an
increase in the annual allocation of fund to NEDFi. The Ministry of DoNER in its Action Taken
Notes has submitted that NEDFi has apprised that the allocated amount would not be sufficient
to meet the financial needs of industrial units in the region for accelerating industrial development
and even the micro-finance and development activities would also scale down. In this backdrop,

45
the Committee strongly reiterates its recommendation made in 210th Report on Demands for
Grants (2018-19) that the Ministry of Finance would give due consideration for higher allocation
to NEDFi from the financial year (2019-20) giving opportunity to boost the pace of economic
development in NER. (Para 3.5.7)
STATUS OF MAJOR ROADS
The Committee notes that there that there has been some progress in the construction of
the various sections of roads such as Melli-Manpur-Namchi, Tarku-Damthang-Namchi and
Nayabazaar-Legship in South and West Sikkim Districts. The Committee notes that no action
has been taken with regard to conducting an audit of construction of neither these roads nor any
explanation from the Sikkim PWD for extremely slow pace of construction has been furnished.
The Committee feels that the construction on these stretches should have been completed by
now. The Committee, therefore strongly reiterates its recommendation for urgently conducting
an audit of construction activities and seeking an explanation from Sikkim PWD for the extremely
snail-pace of the works pertaining to Melli-Manpur-Namchi, Tarku-Damthang-Namchi and
Nayabazaar-Legship roads to fix accountability. The Committee further recommends that the
Ministry of DoNER should form an inspection team of Officers from the Ministries of DoNER
and Road Transport and Highways to visit the project sites by March, 2019 and review the
construction activities of roads. The Ministry desires to be apprised about the detailed findings
of the team at the earliest. (Para 3.6.3)
STATUS OF MAJOR ROADS
The Committee expresses its anguish at the abysmal physical progress of the work
undertaken at various sections of Dimapur-Kohima road for four laning as not even 50%
progress has been achieved on any of the sections with less than a year left in the scheduled date
of completion. The Committee notes that this slow pace of construction is attributable to delay
in shifting of 132 kv HT line tower of Power Grid Corporation of India Limited (PGCIL) and
delay in removal of encumbrances and submission of estimates of additional land. The Committee,
however, feels that these factors should have been taken into account beforehand and tackled
proactively. The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the Ministry of DoNER must
constantly monitor the progress of this project and work with the other agencies concerned to
remove all the bottlenecks so that the project is completed within a set time-frame without any
cost escalation. (Para 3.6.7)
STATUS OF MAJOR ROADS
The Committee expresses its displeasure at the manner in which the road projects are
being planned and executed in the North Eastern region. The Committee notes that the damage
of the Agia-Medhipara-Phulbari-Tura (AMPT) Road, which is a crucial road in Meghalaya, is
mainly due to overloaded trucks plying on the road and the number of commercial vehicle plying
on this road is double the number that was considered in the original design. The Committee is
displeased with the short-sighted planning and non-existent monitoring of the traffic plying on
the road. The Committee recommends that the State Government should fix the accountability

46
for this failure and take necessary action. The Committee further recommends that urgent
measures may be initiated to re-lay the badly damaged parts of this road. The Committee also
recommends that the Ministry of DoNER should review its policy pertaining to roads maintenance/
upgradation that being the responsibility of the State Government concerned and also formulate
certain monitoring mechanism to inspect the condition of roads. The proposed inspection committee
may comprise of officials from both the Central Government and the State Government concerned.
(Para 3.6.11)
TELECOM SECTOR
The Committee takes note of the progress made with regard to the 20 per cent of the
Gram panchayat covered under Bharat Net Phase-I and the target set to cover 4938 Gram
Panchayat in phase-II. The Committee also notes the submission of the Ministry that electricity
is not available in more than 90% of Gram Panchayat locations. The Committee is anguished
at the poor state of infrastructure due to which the connectivity woes of the NER are not being
resolved. The Committee also notes that the Ministry has not provided any details of timeframe
of completion of Bharat Net Phase I and II. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the
Committee may be apprised about the implementation status and completion timeframe of
projects under both the Phases. The Committee also recommends that the Ministry of DoNER
must coordinate with State Governments in NER for removing hindrances faced by the Department
of Telecommunication which inter-alia include site acquisition for Mobile Towers (Assam and
Manipur), electricity Project and Economic Blockade (Manipur) and NOC from DC office (Arunachal
Pradesh, Meghalaya and Mizoram). (Para 3.7.3)
TOURISM
The Committee finds the response of the Ministry of DoNER evasive and unsatisfactory
with regard to the Committee's recommendation for release of the sanctioned amount of
````` 1267.49 crore against which only a sum of ````` 686.19 crore was released under the Swadesh
Darshan Scheme. The Committee strongly feels that the very purpose of creation of the Ministry
of DoNER was to coordinate with other Ministries including the Ministry of Tourism and the
Ministry of Finance regarding various developmental activities of NER. Further recommendation
of the Committee has not been communicated so far rather it is being communicated after so
much time. Therefore, Committee has no option but to reiterate its recommendation.
(Para 3.8.3)
NORTH EASTERN INDUSTRIAL AND INVESTMENT PROMOTION POLICY (NEIIPP)
The Committee notes that Union Cabinet has approved North East Industrial Development
Scheme (NEIDS) 2017, with an outlay of ````` 3,000.00 crore with effect from 1st April, 2017 and
that would remain in force upto 31st March, 2022. The Committee recommends that a strategy
should be chalked out to implement the programme/action plan to boost integrated and balanced
industrialization in NER. The Committee also desires to be apprised in detail about the North
East Industrial Development Scheme (NEIDS) 2017 and a comparative statement of components,

47
scope, and incentives of NEIDS vis-a-vis North East Industrial & Investment Promotion Policy
(NEIIPP), 2007 may be furnished. (Para 3.9.7)
NORTH EASTERN INDUSTRIAL AND INVESTMENT PROMOTION POLICY (NEIIPP)
The Committee further notes that the special scheme for promotion of MSMEs in NER and
Sikkim as approved in 2016, has now been made a component of new Central Sector Scheme
called "Trade and Economic Relations Committee (TERC)". The Committee hopes that necessary
impetus would be given to the promotion of MSMEs under 'TERC' and Capacity Building of
officers and establishment and strengthening of Resource Development Centre (RDC) would be
beneficial in execution of schemes and programmes in NER. However, the Committee observes
that the Ministry has not informed the Committee about the progress and status of implementation
of the projects under the Scheme 'Promotion of MSMEs in NER & Sikkim' and desires to be
apprised about the same. (Para 3.9.8)
AGRICULTURE AND FOOD PROCESSING SECTOR
The Committee notes the trend of allocation of funds to Mission Organic Value Chain
Development (MOVCD) for NER. Against the total budget allocation of ````` 15886.98 lakh in
2015-16, a sum of ````` 11210.99 lakh was released and expended and against the budget allocation
of ````` 10,000.00 lakh in 2016-17, a sum of ````` 4868.42 lakh was released and against budget
allocation of ````` 10,000.00 lakh in 2017-18, a sum of ````` 6648.07 lakh was released. The Committee
notes that against the total fund released to the tune of ````` 22595.57 lakh only a sum of ````` 17791.83
lakh was utilized and a sum of ````` 4803.74 lakh remains unspent balance. The Committee,
therefore, recommends the Ministry to review the implementation status of MOVCD in NER and
undertake appropriate measure to achieve the targets. (Para 3.10.4)
ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS
The Committee notes that NER received a total amount of ````` 52.47 crore for implementation
of National Mission for Green India (GIM). The Committee, however, expresses its displeasure
as no action seems to have been taken for implementation of Committee's recommendation. The
Committee feels that mere allocation and release of funds would not be effective in expanding
the forest cover without robust and effective monitoring, and regular evaluation of the various
components of Green India Mission. The Committee, therefore, reiterates its recommendation
and desires to be apprised about the measures taken in various North Eastern States for providing
training on sustainable agricultural practices, offering alternative livelihood opportunities to the
people living around the forest areas, and intensifying afforestation programmes. The Committee
also desires to be apprised about the various outcomes achieved in different States of the NER
as a result of implementation of Green India Mission. (Para 3.11.4)
INCLUSIVE GROWTH
The Committee notes that various Department/Ministries of the Central Government are
promoting Inclusive Growth in NER through devolution and decentralization of the benefits of

48
undertaken schemes/programmes on the ground level. The Committee has been given to
understand that Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) and Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana
(PMMY) aim at the mission of Financial inclusion and to provide access to institutional Finance
to MSME that would eradicate poverty, remove socio-economic equalities and provide equal
opportunities and distributive justice to the downtrodden people. The Committee observes that
the Ministry of DoNER is coordinating with various Central Government Departments/ Ministries
to re-direct the benefits of various schemes in the upliftment of socio-economic conditions in
NER. The Committee desires to be regularly apprised about the status of implementation of
various ongoing schemes, their outcomes, and the overall impact in achieving inclusive growth
in NER. (Para 3.12.13)
REVENUE SECTION
The Committee would like to be apprised of the budgetary allocation made to the Ministry
of DoNER at RE stage 2018-19 against the projected demand and whether the amount so earmarked
would be sufficient to meet the requirements for various schemes. (Para 4.1.3)
SCHEMES OF NORTH EASTERN COUNCIL
The Committee notes the action taken by the Ministry. But there is no mention as to
whether any special drive has been undertaken to reduce the pendency of UCs. The Committee
therefore, reiterates its recommendation that clearance drives should be carried out to clear the
backlog of UCs. (Para 4.2.3)
KARBI ANGLONG AUTONOMOUS TERRITORIAL COUNCIL (KAATC)
The Committee recommends that since the entire allocation to the tune of ````` 40.00 crore
has been already released now, the Ministry should expeditiously complete all the projects under
KAATC and inform this Committee about the updated status. (Para 4.3.3)
NORTH EAST REGIONAL AGRICULTURAL MARKETING CORPORATION (NERAMAC)
The Committee expresses the urgent need for the revival of the North East Regional
Agricultural Marketing Corporation (NERAMAC) so that the corporation is capable of carrying
out its core activities i.e. creation of a world class infrastructure for processing, value-addition
and marketing of agricultural allied goods in the NER. Since the revival package of NERAMAC
is under consideration, the Committee recommends that the Government must expedite the
approval of revival package of NERAMAC. (Para 4.4.3)
STATUS OF MAJOR ROADS
The Committee strongly recommends that the physical and financial progress of Wokha-
Merapani must be periodically monitored to ensure the completion of construction activities by
March, 2019 at the cost of ````` 154.01 crore. (Para 4.5.3)
CIVIL AVIATION
The Committee desires that the Ministry of DoNER should coordinate with the Ministry
of Civil Aviation and the State Governments concerned and remove the bottlenecks in

49
implementation of smaller projects that are at various stages of completion. The Committee also
desires to be apprised about the physical and financial progress achieved in these projects along
with original and scheduled dates of completion. (Para 4.6.3)
FLOOD CONTROL PROJECTS
The Committee notes that out of the 37 flood control projects, sanctioned under NEC
Scheme 8 projects have been completed during 2017-18. The Committee may be apprised about
the implementation status of the remaining pending projects vis-a-vis the target dates of completion
fixed for them. (Para 4.7.3)
TOURISM
The Committee desires to be apprised whether or not the matter has been discussed with
the State Government of Manipur. The Committee also desires to be apprised about the details
pertaining to the ongoing works and scheduled date of completion of construction/renovation
work of Mahabali Temple. (Para 4.8.3)
Tourism
The Committee desires to be apprised of the allocation of increased amount at RE
2018-19 for the purpose of projecting Majuli Island from erosion along with the sum utilized
during the year and the physical progress achieved against the set target on the project.
(Para 4.8.6)

INTRODUCTION

been authoried by the Committee to submit the Report on its behalf, do hereby present this Two Hundred
Nineteenth Report on Action Taken by Government on the Recommendations/Observations Contained in the

contained in the Report. The Ministry furnished the Action Taken Notes on the said report to the
Committee on 22nd October, 2018.

contained in the said Report of the Committee has been laid on the Table of Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha
on 19th and 18th December, 2018 respectively in pursuant to the direction of Chairman, Rajya Sabha
dated 24th September 2004.

REPORT
The Action Taken Report of the Committee deals with the action taken by the Ministry of Home
Affairs on the recommendations contained in the Two Hundred Thirteenth Report of the Committee on
'Security Situation in the North Eastern States of India'. The Two Hundred Thirteenth Report was
presented to Rajya Sabha/laid on the Table of Lok Sabha, on 19th July, 2018.
2. Action Taken Notes as received from the Ministry of Home Affairs in respect of the recommendations
contained in the Two Hundred Thirteenth Report have been categorized as follows:
Chapter I:  The Recommendations/Observations, which have been accepted by the Government:
Para Nos. 2.1.4, 2.2.3, 2.2.5, 2.2.6, 2.3.14, 2.4.7, 2.5.9, and 2.8.3 (of Two Hundred Thirteenth
Report)
Total recommendations- 8
The Committee is pleased to note that the Ministry has accepted its recommendations as
mentioned in Chapter-I of the Report.
Chapter II:  The Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue
in view of the Government's replies: Para Nos. 2.3.10, 2.6.12, 3.1.6, 3.1.10, 3.1.11, 3.2.3, 3.3.5,
3.3.8, 3.4.6, 3.4.7 and 3.5.5 (ibid)
Total recommendations - 11
The Committee is convinced with the explanations furnished by the Ministry and, therefore,
does not want to pursue the recommendations further.
Chapter III: The Recommendations/Observations in respect of which the Committee is not satisfied
with the replies of the Ministry: Para Nos. 2.7.5, 2.7.6 and 2.7.7  (ibid)
Total recommendations - 3
The Committee expresses its concern over the non-implementation of its recommendations
contained in Chapter-III and desires that the Ministry should furnish convincing action taken steps
in respect of those recommendations.
Chapter IV: The Recommendations/Observations in respect of which final replies of the Government
have not been received: Para No. 2.3.11 (ibid)
Total Recommendations - 1
In respect of 1 recommendation in Chapter-IV, the Ministry has either furnished interim
reply or couched its response in vague terms.
The Committee desires that the Ministry should furnish pointed and detailed Action Taken Notes
in respect of the Observations/Recommendations made in the Report.
3. The details of the ATNs have been analyzed in the succeeding chapters.
